lines.text: The effort of all men is directed towards the banishment
of fear, towards making life transparently clear and con-
trollable in the interests of our desires and plans, towards
the ever-growing strength of human self-security. We are
determined that nothing more shall disturb us or make us
afraid. The modern world has witnessed an astonishing
development of technics and has harnessed technics in the
service of this constant aim. In this mastery of the world by
technical means we see the ever-present temptation to regard
our life as assured, to regard the world as the sphere of our
domination, and to forget the original uncertainty and
questionableness of the structure of our existence: just as the
rich man whose land brought forth plentifully supposed that
the mere possession of the means of subsistence had also
made his life as a whole secure. But God said to him: "Fool!
This night your soul is required of you!" In fact there is no
need to dwell on the point that, in spite of all the perfection
of our technology, nature itself is never fully within man's
control, and that its forces again and again break forth with
destructive violence in natural catastrophes and are con-
stantly evident in tragedy and misfortune. Every newspaper
we pick up bears witness to this. Nevertheless, the general
sense of security is so great that the most insignificant reader,
while being moved, says to himself: that sort of thing cannot
happen to me.
But there is one fact in life which is not to be overcome by
technical means: namely, death. We do not like to speak of it,
as in general we anxiously avoid mentioning what is un-
pleasant and repulsive to us: such things might disturb our
complacency! For this reason we think and speak as little as
possible of this greatest disturbance of all, death. Formerly it
was regarded as a matter of course that man should prepare
himself for death, when it became imminent, and that in such
circumstances he should look to the Church for comfort and
consolation. To-day we try to conceal from people as much
as possible the approach of their end. Why did people
